pedagogy.title: Why Does NEUTRAL Mean Momentum-Only?
pedagogy.content: In a NEUTRAL regime, the market has no strong directional conviction. Pullback strategies — buying dips expecting a bounce — rely on the market wanting to go higher. In NEUTRAL, that upward bias is absent: a dip might just be the start of a larger decline. Momentum and breakout strategies, by contrast, follow stocks that are already showing strength. They work in NEUTRAL because strong names tend to stay strong even when the broad market is undecided. Think of it like surfing: in calm seas (NEUTRAL), you ride the waves that are already forming (momentum), rather than sitting in flat water hoping a wave will come to you (pullback). The minimum R:R of 1.7 ensures each trade pays enough to compensate for the lower win rate that NEUTRAL regimes historically produce.
